# Results — Study 919 (Methodology Shock) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). A **market-model event study**
over a hardcoded calendar of index **rule changes**: for each change we fit
`r_treated = alpha + beta * r_control` on the 250 sessions ending 21 sessions before the
event, then cumulate the abnormal return over the window. Treated/control pairs are
**QQQ/SPY** (Nasdaq-100 rule changes), **SPY/IWM** (S&P eligibility and float rules) and
**IWM/MDY** (Russell reconstitution rules). Daily **total-return** closes (`yfinance`,
`auto_adjust=True`), shared desk cache. One execution lag: the announcement is public at
the close of day 0, the tradable window starts at day **+1**. Costs 5 bps one-way x NAV on
both legs; the short leg pays borrow (50 bps/yr default, swept); the residual `1 - beta`
dollar exposure is financed at an assumed bill rate (200 bps/yr default, swept). As-of
**2026-06-30** (the partial current month is dropped).*

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | n days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| QQQ, SPY, IWM, MDY (+ BIL cash leg) | 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-30 | 8,411 | Fingerprint `547814cd71c7` |

**PROXY / ASSUMPTION — the event list.** The eight rule changes in
[`methodology_shock/data.py`](../methodology_shock/data.py) were transcribed by hand from
index-provider announcements; they are not a machine-readable feed. Three carry an
`exact` date stamp and five an `approximate` one. Two rows are trimmed by the as-of and
the double-counting rule, so **seven** events survive on each leg: the semi-annual
Russell reconstitution goes live in November 2026 (past the as-of, announcement leg only),
and S&P float-adjustment phase 2 was covered by phase 1's press release, so it has no
announcement of its own (effective leg only). The 5 bps cost, the 50 bps/yr borrow and the
200 bps/yr financing rate are also assumptions and are swept below.

**The two legs are NOT independent samples.** Both multiple-share-class rows took effect
on the day they were announced, so **2 of the 7** observations are literally the same
event window on both legs. The legs are reported side by side as a sign check, never
pooled or treated as 14 draws.

**Audit note — one date was wrong.** An earlier build of this calendar dated the 2011
Nasdaq-100 special rebalance to 2011-03-24 and stamped it `exact`. The NASDAQ OMX press
release is dated **2011-04-05** (effective 2011-05-02). The correction flips that event's
announcement-leg CAR from −120 bps to **+36 bps** and moves the pooled announcement leg
from −36.4 bps to −14.1 bps — which is to say, a single mis-transcribed date in a
seven-observation study moved the headline by 22 bps and the era cut by an order of
magnitude. That is the strongest possible argument for the PROXY label on this input.

## The headline — pooled CAR, tradable window [+1, +10]

| Leg | n | Mean CAR | Median | Hit rate | Cross-event *t* | HAC *t* (daily AR) | Placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Announcement** | 7 | **−14.1 bps** | −22.8 | 43% [0.16, 0.75] | −0.30 | −0.30 | **0.802** |
| **Effective** | 7 | **+35.7 bps** | +36.9 | 57% [0.25, 0.84] | +1.16 | +0.86 | **0.541** |

The two legs point in **opposite directions** and neither is distinguishable from noise.
The placebo *p*-values come from 2,000 randomisation draws that replace every real event
date with a random session on the same pair (excluding ±30 sessions around any real
event) and recompute the pooled CAR identically: the observed −14.1 bps sits inside a null
distribution centred at −3.4 bps with a 95% band of **[−129, +124] bps**.

Per-event CARs, announcement leg (`raw` = the unhedged one-for-one difference):

| Event | Date | Pair | beta | CAR | raw | Date stamp |
|---|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| NDX 2011 special rebalance | 2011-04-05 | QQQ/SPY | 1.03 | +36.3 | +54.4 | exact |
| NDX 2023 special rebalance | 2023-07-07 | QQQ/SPY | 1.23 | −157.1 | −48.5 | exact |
| S&P float adjustment, phase 1 | 2004-03-01 | SPY/IWM | 0.68 | −120.1 | +13.8 | approximate |
| S&P multiple-share-class ban | 2017-07-31 | SPY/IWM | 0.48 | +68.8 | +200.3 | exact |
| S&P multiple-share-class reversal | 2023-04-17 | SPY/IWM | 0.81 | +192.5 | +233.2 | approximate |
| Russell banding | 2007-04-13 | IWM/MDY | 1.22 | −96.2 | −59.5 | approximate |
| Russell semi-annual reconstitution | 2023-09-14 | IWM/MDY | 1.07 | −22.8 | −70.9 | approximate |

Note how far the beta-adjusted CAR can sit from the raw difference (float phase 1:
−120 vs +14 bps). SPY's beta to IWM is only 0.48–0.81, so an unhedged pair mostly measures
the market. That gap is the single largest methodological choice in this study, and it is
the reason the tradable arm below is **beta-hedged**.

## Confidence intervals

| Leg | Mean CAR | Event bootstrap 95% CI | Block bootstrap 95% CI |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Announcement | −14.1 bps | [−93, +73] | [−108, +79] |
| Effective | +35.7 bps | [−15, +96] | [−42, +114] |

Both intervals straddle zero on both legs. The event bootstrap resamples the seven CARs
(events years apart are the natural independent unit); the block bootstrap resamples
5-day blocks of the pooled daily abnormal returns and scales to a 10-day CAR.

## What this sample could ever have detected

With seven events and a cross-event CAR dispersion of 123 bps, the smallest pooled CAR
this design could have called significant at 5% is **≈114 bps** (announcement leg; ≈75 bps
on the effective leg, whose CARs happen to be less dispersed). The placebo distribution
agrees from the other direction: its 95% band is ±~127 bps. **A genuine 20–40 bps
front-running edge would have been invisible here.** The honest reading is therefore not
"there is no effect" but "there is no effect anywhere near the size the folklore implies,
and a small one could not be resolved."

## Window sweep (announcement leg) — nine windows, none survive

| Window | Kind | Mean CAR | Cross-event *t* | Hit | Placebo *p* | Bonferroni *p* |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| [−5,−1] | descriptive | −33.2 | **−3.43** | 14% | 0.451 | 1.000 |
| [−1,+1] | descriptive | −7.7 | −0.49 | 57% | 0.805 | 1.000 |
| [−5,+5] | descriptive | −49.7 | −1.90 | 14% | 0.423 | 1.000 |
| [−10,+10] | descriptive | +4.7 | +0.08 | 57% | 0.961 | 1.000 |
| [+1,+1] | tradable | +5.4 | +0.61 | 57% | 0.799 | 1.000 |
| [+1,+3] | tradable | −14.0 | −0.85 | 29% | 0.654 | 1.000 |
| [+1,+5] | tradable | −6.5 | −0.34 | 43% | 0.874 | 1.000 |
| [+1,+10] | tradable | −14.1 | −0.30 | 43% | 0.802 | 1.000 |
| [+1,+21] | tradable | −57.3 | −0.88 | 43% | 0.498 | 1.000 |

The `[−5,−1]` row is the study's best cautionary tale. Its naive cross-event *t* of
**−3.43** looks like a significant pre-announcement drift — and it is an artefact: with
seven observations the *t*-statistic estimates its own denominator from seven points, and
those seven happened to cluster tightly. The randomisation test, which knows the true
dispersion of a 5-day CAR on this tape, prices the same −33 bps at **p = 0.451**. Nine
windows were examined; the smallest raw *p* anywhere is 0.423, and after Bonferroni
**every** adjusted *p* is 1.000. Windows starting at day 0 or earlier are labelled
*descriptive*: they use information that was not actionable and are not tradable claims.

## Drop-one jackknife (announcement leg, [+1,+10])

| Dropped | CAR without it | *t* without it | Its own CAR |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| NDX 2011 special rebalance | −22.5 | −0.42 | +36.3 |
| NDX 2023 special rebalance | +9.7 | +0.21 | −157.1 |
| S&P float adjustment, phase 1 | +3.6 | +0.07 | −120.1 |
| S&P multiple-share-class ban | −27.9 | −0.53 | +68.8 |
| S&P multiple-share-class reversal | −48.5 | −1.32 | +192.5 |
| Russell banding | −0.4 | −0.01 | −96.2 |
| Russell semi-annual reconstitution | −12.6 | −0.23 | −22.8 |

Dropping any single event swings the pooled CAR anywhere between −48.5 and +9.7 bps — it
even changes sign. No |*t*| gets past 1.32 in any of the seven sub-samples. That is how
fragile a seven-observation mean is, and it is why the |*t*| ≥ 2 bar is applied to the
placebo-priced number rather than to a cross-event *t*.

## Era cut (split 2015-01-01, announcement leg)

| Era | n | Mean CAR | Cross-event *t* | Hit |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Pre-2015 | 3 | −60.0 bps | −1.23 | 33% |
| 2015→ | 4 | +20.4 bps | +0.28 | 50% |

The two eras disagree in sign and neither half is significant. With n = 3 on one side, the
era cut is reported because the house style requires it, not because three observations
can decide anything.

## The tradable arm — beta-hedged pair, on at +1, off at +10

Long 1 unit of the treated wrapper, short `beta` units of the sibling (beta from the same
clean pre-event window), 5 bps one-way x NAV on both legs in and out, borrow 50 bps/yr on
the short notional, and the residual `1 - beta` dollar exposure financed at 200 bps/yr.

**On "excess-of-cash": the beta-hedged pair is not dollar-neutral.** Long 1, short `beta`
leaves `1 - beta` units of NAV as a genuine net position — net **long** +0.52 on the
share-class-ban event (beta 0.48), net **short** −0.23 on NDX 2023 (beta 1.23). Only the
naive 1×/1× variant finances itself exactly. That residual is therefore charged (or
credited) at the bill rate, which is what makes the number below an excess-of-cash return
rather than one merely asserted to be. It is small — mean +0.52 bps at 200 bps/yr — but
it is charged, and it is swept.

| Arm | n | Gross | Net | *t* (net) | Win rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Announcement leg, beta-hedged** | 7 | **−7.7 bps** | **−29.3 bps** | −0.62 | 43% |
| Announcement leg, naive 1x/1x | 7 | +46.2 bps | +24.3 bps | +0.51 | 43% |
| Effective leg, beta-hedged | 7 | +43.2 bps | +21.8 bps | +0.70 | 43% |

The naive dollar-neutral variant looks better only because it is not hedged: its +46 bps is
residual market exposure, not a rule-change effect. **The hedged trade is negative before a
single basis point of cost is charged**, and no arm gets within a mile of |*t*| ≥ 2.

### Cost x borrow sweep (announcement leg, mean net bps)

| One-way cost \\ borrow | 0 bps/yr | 50 | 100 | 300 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0 bps** | −8.2 | −10.0 | −11.8 | −18.9 |
| **1 bps** | −12.0 | −13.8 | −15.6 | −22.8 |
| **5 bps** | −27.5 | −29.3 | −31.1 | −38.2 |
| **10 bps** | −46.8 | −48.6 | −50.4 | −57.5 |
| **25 bps** | −104.8 | −106.6 | −108.4 | −115.5 |

Every cell is negative. Borrow barely matters at a ten-day horizon (a 300 bps/yr rate costs
~11 bps over the hold); the cost of crossing four spreads matters far more. The only
|*t*| ≥ 2 on the tradable arm appears in the bottom row (−2.11 to −2.30) and it says the
trade reliably **loses** money at 25 bps.

### Financing sweep (bill rate on the residual `1 - beta` exposure)

| Rate | Mean charge | Mean net | *t* (net) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps/yr | +0.00 bps | −28.8 | −0.60 |
| 200 bps/yr | +0.52 bps | −29.3 | −0.62 |
| 500 bps/yr | +1.30 bps | −30.1 | −0.64 |

The residual exposure nets close to flat across the seven events (net long on the SPY/IWM
rows, net short on the QQQ/SPY and IWM/MDY rows), so this is a small correction. It is
made explicitly rather than assumed away.

## Deployed-capital race (excess-of-cash)

Park the NAV in **BIL** and overlay the pair only inside event windows. BIL starts on
2007-05-30, so **5 of the 7 announcement events land inside the cash era and 2 are
dropped** — the 2004 float-adjustment announcement and the 2007 Russell banding
announcement, both of which happen to be losers. They are *dropped*, not mapped onto BIL's
first session; an earlier build did the latter and manufactured a −3.8% drawdown in the
first ten days of the cash era out of two events that predate it.

| | |
|---|---|
| Live days | 50 of 4,802 |
| Total excess return | **+65 bps** over nineteen years |
| Overlay excess-of-cash Sharpe | **+0.187** (HAC *t* = +0.37), vol 0.18%, max DD −2.16% |
| SPY excess-of-cash Sharpe, same window | **+0.542** |

Read this the right way round. The overlay is *positive* here only because the cash era
excludes the two pre-2007 losers; on the full seven-event list the same trade averages
−29.3 bps net. Five trades in nineteen years producing +65 bps — about 3 bps a year, with
a HAC *t* of +0.37 — is a rounding error, not an edge, and it is a third of SPY's
risk-adjusted return for a strategy that is idle 99% of the time.

## Synthetic control (machinery proof — never supports the stamp)

On a planted world (three synthetic pairs, twelve announcements, a **+250 bps** abnormal
drift bled in over the ten sessions after each) the detector recovers **+314.9 bps**
(cross-event *t* = +3.21, placebo *p* = 0.000, hit rate 92%). On the matched null it
recovers +64.9 bps with placebo *p* = 0.270, and across six independent null seeds the
pooled CAR averages **+17.4 bps (sd 53.5)** — centred on zero. The harness is powered and
unbiased; the flat real-tape result is a property of the tape, not of the code.

## Verdict

- **Signal — None.** Neither leg of the event study produces a CAR distinguishable from
  its own placebo distribution: **−14.1 bps (p = 0.802)** on announcement, **+35.7 bps
  (p = 0.541)** on effective, with **opposite signs**. The smallest placebo *p* across
  nine windows is 0.423 and every Bonferroni-adjusted *p* is 1.000. Both bootstrap CIs
  straddle zero, the two eras disagree in sign, dropping any one event swings the pooled
  CAR through zero, and the only apparently significant *t* in the study (−3.43 in the
  pre-announcement window) is dismantled by the randomisation test. Nothing here clears
  the desk's |*t*| ≥ 2 bar on the real tape. **Survivorship: none to name** — four
  continuously listed wrappers chosen ex ante by the index each tracks; the selection risk
  lives entirely in the hand-assembled event list, which is why the jackknife, the window
  sweep and the placebo test are all reported — and why one corrected date is documented
  above rather than quietly absorbed.
- **Tradability — Mirage.** The beta-hedged pair loses **−7.7 bps gross** and −29.3 bps
  net per event (*t* = −0.62, 43% win rate); **every** cell of the cost × borrow sweep is
  negative, including the zero-cost corner. The one version that looks profitable
  (+24 bps net, naive 1×/1×) is unhedged market beta wearing a costume. The
  deployed-capital overlay's +65 bps over nineteen years is five post-2007 trades' worth
  of noise (HAC *t* = +0.37, Sharpe +0.19 against SPY's +0.54) on a sub-sample that
  excludes two losers, not a bankable return.
- **What the study can and cannot say.** With seven events the minimum detectable CAR is
  ~114 bps. A real but modest 20–40 bps rule-change footprint — the size the mechanism
  would plausibly produce at the *wrapper* level, where a basket-wide reweighting is
  diluted across hundreds of names — would be invisible to this design. The claim that
  survives is the tradable one: **at the wrapper level there is no front-runnable
  methodology shock large enough to pay for the spread**, which is the only version of the
  claim a price-taker could act on.
